name: C2 Family Reunification Visa

requirements.blocker_text: Under Article 27 of Kazakhstan's Migration Law, the sponsor must be a Kazakhstani citizen, a foreign residence-permit holder, an ethnic Kazakh/former compatriot with 2+ years on a temporary residence permit, or a business immigrant with 1+ year continuous residence. Eligible family members: spouses married 1+ year (civil partnerships not recognized), unmarried children under 18, financially-dependent unmarried adult children with a health-based justification, dependent disabled parents, and other dependents whose support falls on the sponsor. Housing of at least 15 sq. meters per person and bank proof of minimum-wage-level funds per family member are also required.
requirements.fix_path: Confirm the sponsor qualifies and gather the marriage/birth certificates, housing, and financial proof required for the C2 visa.

evidence_required.document: Bank certificate showing minimum-wage funds per family member

outcome.duration_length: single-entry up to 90 days; multiple-entry up to 1 year or the sponsor's residence-permit duration

sources.title: DOS Immigration (Kazakhstan-focused immigration consultancy) -- describes the C2 family-reunification visa under Article 27 of Kazakhstan's Migration Law: qualifying sponsors, eligible family members, required documents (housing, financial, medical, police), and visa duration

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Kazakhstan). STATUS: DRAFT -- sourced to a private immigration consultancy (tier 3) citing Kazakhstan's Migration Law Article 27, not the primary legal text itself (Kazakhstan's Adilet legal database likely hosts it but was not located/fetched for this specific article in this build). GENUINE, SPECIFIC FINDING: the one-year minimum marriage duration and explicit non-recognition of civil partnerships are concrete, sourced conditions, not vague gaps. SEPARATE, RELATED FINDING NOT MODELED IN THIS FILE: per kz_international_protection.json, recognized refugees in Kazakhstan have a distinct, UNHCR-confirmed (tier 2) family-reunification right for spouse and dependent children under the refugee-status framework specifically, which may operate on different terms than this general C2 visa -- not merged here to avoid overstating either mechanism's scope. study_rights set 'restricted' since no explicit school-enrollment right for dependents was detailed in the source reviewed.
